steps.intro: This is Moon Run, our crew's game. Watch it play. Is something missing?

steps.prompt: What is missing from Moon Run?
steps.reveal: Moon Run has no sounds at all. No jump, no bump, no music. Our crew is going to make every one of them!

steps.title: Games used to bleep!
steps.text: Old game machines had a tiny sound chip inside. It could only make a few simple sounds at once. Music made with those chips is called chiptune.

art.credit: Game Boy. Photo: Evan-Amos, public domain

wow.text: The Game Boy came out in 1989. That's about 37 years ago: more than six times as long as {commander} has been alive.

steps.dad: Ask: did you ever play on one of these?

steps.title: A band of four
steps.text: The NES could play just four main sounds at once. That's like a band with only four players.

art.alt: A Nintendo Entertainment System with a controller

wow.text: Its four were two beepy square sounds, one soft triangle sound and one hissy noise sound.

steps.intro: Our four robots are asleep! {copilot}, tap each one to wake it up.

steps.title: Every bot sounds different
steps.text: Bleep is beepy. Hoot is soft. Buzz is buzzy. Fizz is hissy, like the sea.

steps.prompt: Which robot sounds like a buzzy bee?
steps.reveal: It's Buzz! Buzz makes a bright, buzzy sound. Its wave looks like the teeth of a saw.

steps.prompt: Which robot has the softest sound?
steps.reveal: Hoot! Hoot's sound is soft and sweet, a bit like a flute.

steps.intro: Close your eyes! One of you taps a secret robot. The other listens and guesses who sang.
When our robot bumps a rock, somebody should say bonk! Tap each robot to hear its bonk. {commander}, you choose.
Try it! Bump into a rock and listen for your bonk.

debrief: Which robot is your favourite, and why?
{engineer}, did your games go bleep when you were little?
